checks: Matched source 9764a982661d3ddc §5 and equation (5) to the exact finite roof, its affine extension and the convex gap test. The source digest matches.

Every convex combination of chosen support maximizers belongs to C. When its base is sampled, exactness puts it in K_z and bounds its height by h_z. The one-site representation gives equality at every sampled site, including a nonvertex site.

The downward hull is a closed polyhedron of dimension dim aff(P)+1 in its relative ambient space. Downward recession forces the height coefficient of any outward facet inequality to be nonnegative. Vertical facets only constrain the base. At least one upper inequality is needed because every roof value is finite. The minimum of the nonvertical affine upper bounds is therefore the exact roof on conv(P), including relative boundary bases.

Affinely extending the finitely many upper bounds gives a globally finite concave minimum, also when the base rank is zero. All points of C have physical height at most this roof by convex combination of the sampled height bounds.

The finite convex test u·X−h̃(z) is integrable on the compact hull for the finite measures of convex order. It is nonpositive there and vanishes on the old law, so convex order forces vanishing almost everywhere for the new law. At sampled sites this is exactly the support equality.

overlap.comparison: The three-fiber martingale derives tightness from its base-zero mean at a fixed middle site. It does not provide a finite sampled roof or contact preservation for arbitrary convex-ordered laws across changing base pairs.

This also uses minima of affine functions on compatible sampled fibers, but constructs entropy-optimal height profiles and gives their sensitivity. It does not give the support-function roof or its contact-transfer conclusion.
